expertNames: Lisa Wayne, Lenore Walker, Susan Criss, Chris Voss, BJ Fogg

intake.situation: I called 911 because my husband was threatening me and when the police arrived, HE told them I hit him. They arrested me instead. My public defender barely talks to me — he met me once for five minutes and said 'these cases usually plead out.' I have a protective order against ME now, so I can't go home. I'm staying with my sister. I didn't do anything wrong but nobody is listening to me.
intake.specific_question: How can I be the one arrested when I'm the one who called 911? Does that matter legally? And can the protective order be modified so I can at least get my things from the house?

charge_specific_data.injuries_to_defendant: bruising on defendant's arms and neck (documented at booking)
charge_specific_data.children_present: yes — two children (ages 4 and 7) were in the home
charge_specific_data.protective_order: emergency protective order issued against defendant
charge_specific_data.mandatory_arrest: yes — Texas mandatory arrest policy for DV calls

phase2_data.biggest_concern: I can't see my kids. Roberto has them and he's using this to control me. I'm terrified he'll get full custody and I'll never get them back.
phase2_data.what_attorney_told: He said these cases usually plead out and I should think about it
phase2_data.employment: Elementary school teacher — currently on administrative leave pending case resolution
